    <div class="callouts">
      <div class="callout ghost">
        <div class="eyebrow">Design Decision 
 Ghost</div>
        <h3>35% opacity + 2
 rotation</h3>
        <p>The dragged item fades to <code>opacity: 0.35</code> in-place and tilts <code>2deg</code> clockwise. This signals "I've been picked up" without the jarring flash of a fully-invisible source. The slight tilt adds physicality 
 it feels like lifting a sticky note off a board.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="callout indicator">
        <div class="eyebrow">Design Decision 
 Drop Indicator</div>
        <h3>Indigo line + dot endpoint</h3>
        <p>A 2px <code>indigo-5</code> line appears between items to show exactly where the drop will land. The dot on the left end anchors the eye. We avoid highlighting the entire gap (too heavy) or using a border on the target item (ambiguous direction).</p>
      </div>
      <div class="callout snap">
        <div class="eyebrow">Design Decision 
 Snap Behavior</div>
        <h3>Items reflow instantly, no animation</h3>
        <p>During drag, items shift position without transition. Animated reflows during drag feel "laggy" 
 the user is already focused on their cursor, so instant snaps feel more responsive. The final drop <em>does</em> get a subtle 120ms ease-out.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="callout timing">
        <div class="eyebrow">Design Decision 
 Drag Threshold</div>
        <h3>No hold delay, immediate grab</h3>
        <p>We use the native HTML5 drag API with no artificial delay. The 6-dot grip pattern on hover signals draggability. On touch devices we'd add a <code>150ms</code> long-press threshold, but this prototype targets desktop cursor interaction only.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <!-- Open Questions -->
  <div class="questions">
    <div class="eyebrow">Open Questions</div>
    <h2>Unresolved Design Decisions</h2>
    <div class="q-item">
      <div class="q-num">1</div>
      <div class="q-body">
        <strong>Should reordering persist immediately or require a save action?</strong>
        <p>Auto-save feels modern but could frustrate users who accidentally drag. A "Reset to default" option in Settings might be enough of a safety net.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="q-item">
      <div class="q-num">2</div>
      <div class="q-body">
        <strong>Keyboard-accessible reorder?</strong>
        <p>Power users expect <code>Alt+
</code> to move items. This is straightforward to implement but needs clear focus styling that doesn't conflict with the drag states.</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="q-item">
      <div class="q-num">3</div>
      <div class="q-body">
        <strong>Pin/lock items to prevent accidental moves?</strong>
        <p>Dashboard and Settings feel like fixtures. Should we allow pinning items so they can't be dragged? This adds UI complexity (pin icon, locked state styling).</p>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="q-item">
      <div class="q-num">4</div>
      <div class="q-body">
        <strong>Mobile touch behavior?</strong>
        <p>HTML5 Drag and Drop has spotty mobile support. If mobile matters, we'd need a touch-based implementation with long-press activation. Should we scope this prototype to desktop only?</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>

<script>
const navList = document.getElementById('navList');
let draggedItem = null;
let placeholder = null;
function createIndicator() {
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.className = 'drop-indicator';
  el.style.display = 'block';
  return el;
function updateOrderDisplay() {
  const items = navList.querySelectorAll('.nav-item');
  const ids = Array.from(items).map(function(item) { return item.dataset.id; });
  document.getElementById('orderDisplay').textContent = 'Order: ' + ids.join(' 
 ');
navList.addEventListener('dragstart', function(e) {
  const item = e.target.closest('.nav-item');
  if (!item) return;
  draggedItem = item;
  placeholder = createIndicator();
  setTimeout(function() {
    item.classList.add('dragging');
  }, 0);
  e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move';
  e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', item.dataset.id);
  // ghost image with opacity
  if (e.dataTransfer.setDragImage) {
    const clone = item.cloneNode(true);
    clone.style.position = 'absolute';
    clone.style.top = '-1000px';
    clone.style.opacity = '0.7';
    clone.style.transform = 'rotate(2deg)';
    clone.style.width = item.offsetWidth + 'px';
    document.body.appendChild(clone);
    e.dataTransfer.setDragImage(clone, 20, 20);
    setTimeout(function() { document.body.removeChild(clone); }, 0);
navList.addEventListener('dragover', function(e) {
  e.preventDefault();
  e.dataTransfer.dropEffect = 'move';
  if (!draggedItem) return;
  // Remove existing placeholder
  if (placeholder.parentNode) placeholder.parentNode.removeChild(placeholder);
  const afterElement = getDragAfterElement(navList, e.clientY);
  if (afterElement) {
    navList.insertBefore(placeholder, afterElement);
  } else {
    navList.appendChild(placeholder);
navList.addEventListener('dragend', function(e) {
  if (!draggedItem) return;
  draggedItem.classList.remove('dragging');
  // Place item where the indicator is
  if (placeholder.parentNode) {
    navList.insertBefore(draggedItem, placeholder);
    placeholder.parentNode.removeChild(placeholder);
  // Subtle settle animation
  draggedItem.style.transition = 'transform 120ms ease-out, opacity 120ms ease-out';
  draggedItem.style.transform = 'scale(1.02)';
  draggedItem.style.opacity = '0.8';
  setTimeout(function() {
    draggedItem.style.transform = '';
    draggedItem.style.opacity = '';
    setTimeout(function() {
      draggedItem.style.transition = '';
    }, 120);
  }, 10);
  draggedItem = null;
  updateOrderDisplay();
navList.addEventListener('dragleave', function(e) {
  // Only remove if leaving the list entirely
  if (!navList.contains(e.relatedTarget) && placeholder.parentNode) {
    placeholder.parentNode.removeChild(placeholder);
function getDragAfterElement(container, y) {
  const elements = Array.from(container.querySelectorAll('.nav-item:not(.dragging)'));
  return elements.reduce(function(closest, child) {
    const box = child.getBoundingClientRect();
    const offset = y - box.top - box.height / 2;
    if (offset < 0 && offset > closest.offset) {
      return { offset: offset, element: child };
    }
    return closest;
  }, { offset: Number.NEGATIVE_INFINITY }).element;
</script>

<script>
function downloadSVG(id, filename) {
  const svg = document.getElementById(id);
  const clone = svg.cloneNode(true);
  const styles = getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
  const varsUsed = [
    '--color-background-primary','--color-background-secondary','--color-border-tertiary',
    '--color-sky-1','--color-sky-2','--color-sky-3','--color-sky-5','--color-sky-7','--color-sky-9',
    '--color-amber-1','--color-amber-2','--color-amber-3','--color-amber-5','--color-amber-7','--color-amber-9',
    '--color-mint-1','--color-mint-2','--color-mint-5','--color-mint-7',
    '--color-coral-1','--color-coral-5','--color-coral-7',
    '--color-text-tertiary',
  ];
  let svgStr = new XMLSerializer().serializeToString(clone);
  varsUsed.forEach(v => {
    const val = styles.getPropertyValue(v).trim();
    svgStr = svgStr.replaceAll(`var(${v})`, val);
  });
  const blob = new Blob([svgStr], { type: 'image/svg+xml' });
  const a = document.createElement('a');
  a.href = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  a.download = filename;
  a.click();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(a.href);
</script>

<script>
const steps = {
  push: { title:'git push', desc:'Developer pushes to main or opens a PR. Webhook triggers CI pipeline via GitHub Actions.', tags:[{t:'~2s',c:'time'},{t:'trigger',c:'pass'}] },
  ci: { title:'CI Init', desc:'Checkout code, restore caches (node_modules, Cargo target), detect affected packages in monorepo using Nx.', tags:[{t:'~30s',c:'time'}] },
  tests: { title:'Tests (Lint + Unit + Integration)', desc:'Run ESLint, rustfmt, cargo test, vitest in parallel across affected packages. Fail-fast on first error.', tags:[{t:'~4min',c:'time'},{t:'pass 
 build',c:'pass'},{t:'fail 
 notify',c:'fail'}] },
  build: { title:'Build Artifacts', desc:'Compile Rust binaries (release mode), bundle JS/TS with esbuild, build Docker images. Outputs stored in artifact registry.', tags:[{t:'~6min',c:'time'}] },
  canary: { title:'Canary Deploy (5%)', desc:'Deploy to 5% of traffic. Monitor error rate, p99 latency, and memory for 10 minutes. Auto-rollback if SLO breached.', tags:[{t:'~12min',c:'time'},{t:'fail 
 rollback',c:'fail'}] },
  promote: { title:'Promote to 100%', desc:'Gradually shift traffic 5% 
 25% 
 50% 
 100% over 20 minutes. Each step validates health checks.', tags:[{t:'~20min',c:'time'}] },
  smoke: { title:'Smoke Tests', desc:'Run critical-path E2E tests against production: login flow, API key generation, agent chat roundtrip.', tags:[{t:'~3min',c:'time'},{t:'pass 
 done',c:'pass'},{t:'fail 
 rollback',c:'fail'}] },
  done: { title:'Pipeline Complete 
', desc:'All checks passed. Slack notification sent. Deployment tagged in GitHub release.', tags:[{t:'total ~45min',c:'time'},{t:'success',c:'pass'}] },
function show(key) {
  const s = steps[key];
  if (!s) return;
  document.getElementById('detailTitle').textContent = s.title;
  document.getElementById('detailDesc').textContent = s.desc;
  const tagsEl = document.getElementById('detailTags');
  tagsEl.innerHTML = s.tags.map(t =>
    `<span class="tag tag-${t.c}">${t.t}</span>`
  ).join('');
  const panel = document.getElementById('detailPanel');
  const colors = { push:'--color-sky-5', ci:'--color-indigo-5', tests:'--color-amber-5', build:'--color-violet-5', canary:'--color-amber-5', promote:'--color-mint-5', smoke:'--color-amber-5', done:'--color-mint-5' };
  panel.style.borderLeftColor = `var(${colors[key] || '--color-indigo-5'})`;
</script>

  <div class="eyebrow" style="color:var(--color-indigo-5);">Feature Explainer</div>
  <h1>How Rate Limiting Works in This API</h1>
  <p class="subtitle">Token-bucket algorithm with per-tenant quotas and graceful degradation.</p>
  <!-- TL;DR -->
  <div class="tldr">
    <div class="eyebrow">TL;DR</div>
    <p>Every API request passes through a <strong>token-bucket rate limiter</strong> keyed by tenant ID. Each tenant gets a configurable burst capacity and steady refill rate. When the bucket is empty, requests receive a <code>429 Too Many Requests</code> with a <code>Retry-After</code> header. Premium tiers get higher limits. The limiter runs as middleware before any business logic executes.</p>
  </div>
  <!-- Steps -->
  <div class="eyebrow" style="color:var(--color-teal-7);">How It Works</div>
  <div class="section-label">Request Path (4 Steps)</div>
  <div class="steps-container">
    <div class="step open">
      <div class="step-header" onclick="toggleStep(this)">
        <div class="step-num">1</div>
        <div class="step-title">Request arrives at API Gateway</div>
        <div class="step-chevron">
</div>
      </div>
      <div class="step-body">
        The gateway extracts the <code>X-Tenant-ID</code> header (or derives it from the API key). This becomes the rate-limit key. If no tenant ID is found, the request is rejected with <code>401 Unauthorized</code> before reaching the limiter.
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="step">
      <div class="step-header" onclick="toggleStep(this)">
        <div class="step-num">2</div>
        <div class="step-title">Token bucket check (Redis)</div>
        <div class="step-chevron">
</div>
      </div>
      <div class="step-body">
        The middleware calls <code>EVALSHA</code> on a Lua script in Redis that atomically: (a) refills tokens based on elapsed time since last request, (b) checks if 
1 token is available, (c) decrements the counter. The bucket parameters come from config: <code>burst=100, refill_rate=10/s</code> for standard tier.
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="step">
      <div class="step-header" onclick="toggleStep(this)">
        <div class="step-num">3</div>
        <div class="step-title">Decision: allow or throttle</div>
        <div class="step-chevron">
</div>
      </div>
      <div class="step-body">
        If tokens are available, the request proceeds to the handler. Response headers include <code>X-RateLimit-Remaining</code> and <code>X-RateLimit-Reset</code>. If the bucket is empty, a <code>429</code> response is returned immediately with <code>Retry-After: {seconds}</code> computed from the refill rate.
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="step">
      <div class="step-header" onclick="toggleStep(this)">
        <div class="step-num">4</div>
        <div class="step-title">Graceful degradation mode</div>
        <div class="step-chevron">
</div>
      </div>
      <div class="step-body">
        If Redis is unreachable, the limiter falls back to an in-memory counter with a <code>2
 conservative limit</code>. A circuit breaker monitors Redis health and auto-recovers. During degradation, the <code>X-RateLimit-Source: local</code> header is set so clients can detect the fallback.
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
  <!-- Code tabs -->
  <div class="tabs-section">
    <div class="eyebrow" style="color:var(--color-violet-7);">Code Examples</div>
    <div class="section-label">Configuration & Implementation</div>
    <div class="tab-bar">
      <button class="tab-btn active" onclick="switchTab(0)">YAML Config</button>
      <button class="tab-btn" onclick="switchTab(1)">Route Code</button>
      <button class="tab-btn" onclick="switchTab(2)">Client Response</button>
    </div>
    <div class="tab-panel active" data-tab="0">
<pre>rate_limit:
  default_tier:
    burst: 100            # max tokens in bucket
    refill_rate: 10       # tokens per second
    refill_interval: 100ms
  premium_tier:
    burst: 500
    refill_rate: 50
    refill_interval: 100ms
  redis:
    cluster: rate-limit-cluster
    key_prefix: "rl:v2:"
    ttl: 3600s
  fallback:
    enabled: true
    local_limit_multiplier: 0.5</pre>
    </div>
    <div class="tab-panel" data-tab="1">
<pre>// middleware/rate_limit.go
func RateLimitMiddleware(cfg *RateLimitConfig) gin.HandlerFunc {
    return func(c *gin.Context) {
        tenantID := c.GetHeader("X-Tenant-ID")
        if tenantID == "" {
            c.AbortWithStatusJSON(401, ErrNoTenant)
            return
        }
        bucket := cfg.GetBucket(tenantID)
        allowed, remaining, resetAt := bucket.Allow()
        c.Header("X-RateLimit-Remaining",
            strconv.Itoa(remaining))
        c.Header("X-RateLimit-Reset",
            strconv.FormatInt(resetAt.Unix(), 10))
        if !allowed {
            retryAfter := time.Until(resetAt).Seconds()
            c.Header("Retry-After",
                strconv.Itoa(int(retryAfter)))
            c.AbortWithStatusJSON(429, ErrRateLimited)
            return
        }
        c.Next()
    }
}</pre>
    </div>
    <div class="tab-panel" data-tab="2">
<pre>HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 6
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1747420800
  "error": {
    "code": "RATE_LIMITED",
    "message": "Request rate exceeded. Try again in 6s.",
    "tenant_id": "tenant_abc123",
    "tier": "default",
    "docs": "https://docs.api.dev/rate-limits"
}</pre>
    </div>
  </div>
  <!-- Gotchas -->
  <div class="gotchas">
    <div class="eyebrow" style="color:var(--color-amber-7);">Gotchas</div>
    <div class="section-label">Common Pitfalls</div>
    <div class="gotcha-card">
      <h4>
 Clock skew between Redis nodes</h4>
      <p>Token refill uses Redis server time (<code>redis.time()</code>), not client time. If your Redis cluster has clock drift &gt;100ms, buckets may refill unevenly. Use NTP sync on all nodes.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="gotcha-card">
      <h4>
 Burst 
 sustained throughput</h4>
      <p>A burst of 100 means 100 requests can fire instantly, but the sustained rate is only <code>refill_rate</code> (10/s). Don't confuse burst capacity with steady-state QPS.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="gotcha-card">
      <h4>
 Retry-After is approximate</h4>
      <p>The <code>Retry-After</code> header rounds up to the nearest second. Clients should add 100-500ms jitter to avoid thundering herd on retry.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <!-- FAQ -->
  <div class="faq">
    <div class="eyebrow" style="color:var(--color-mint-7);">FAQ</div>
    <div class="section-label">Frequently Asked Questions</div>
    <div class="faq-item">
      <div class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFaq(this)">Can I get a higher rate limit for my tenant?</div>
      <div class="faq-a">Yes. Contact the platform team via <code>#platform-eng</code> on Lark. Premium tier provides 5
 the default limits. Enterprise customers can request custom quotas via the admin console.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="faq-item">
      <div class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFaq(this)">What happens during Redis failover?</div>
      <div class="faq-a">The circuit breaker detects Redis unavailability within 3 failed health checks (~1.5s). It switches to local in-memory counting with 50% of the configured limit (conservative). When Redis recovers, the circuit breaker auto-resets after 5 consecutive successful checks.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="faq-item">
      <div class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFaq(this)">Are WebSocket connections rate-limited?</div>
      <div class="faq-a">WebSocket <strong>upgrades</strong> are rate-limited (counts as 1 request). Once connected, individual messages are not token-bucketed 
 they use a separate message-rate limiter with a sliding window of 60 messages/minute.</div>
    </div>
    <div class="faq-item">
      <div class="faq-q" onclick="toggleFaq(this)">How do I monitor my usage?</div>
      <div class="faq-a">Check the <code>X-RateLimit-Remaining</code> response header on every request. For dashboards, query the <code>rate_limit_consumption</code> metric in Grafana filtered by <code>tenant_id</code>. Alerts fire when remaining drops below 10% of burst.</div>
    </div>
  </div>

<div class="panel">
  <header>
    <div class="eyebrow">Concept Deep-Dive</div>
    <h1>Consistent Hashing</h1>
    <p>How distributed systems map keys to nodes without rehashing everything when topology changes.</p>
  </header>
  <div class="layout">
    <div class="main">
      <p style="font-size:14px;color:var(--color-text-secondary);margin-bottom:12px;">
        A <span class="term" data-term="hash-ring">hash ring</span> maps both
        <span class="term" data-term="node">nodes</span> and
        <span class="term" data-term="key">keys</span> onto a circular space.
        Each key is served by the first node encountered clockwise 
 its
        <span class="term" data-term="successor">successor</span>.
        When a node joins or leaves, only keys in its
        <span class="term" data-term="partition">partition</span> are remapped.
      </p>
      <div class="node-count" id="nodeCount">Nodes on ring: 3</div>
      <svg class="ring-svg" id="ringSvg" width="340" height="340" viewBox="0 0 340 340"></svg>
      <div class="controls">
        <button onclick="addNode()">+ Add Node</button>
        <button class="remove" onclick="removeNode()">
 Remove Node</button>
      </div>
      <div class="comparison">
        <div class="eyebrow" style="margin-bottom:10px;">Comparison 
 Consistent vs Mod-N</div>
        <table>
          <thead><tr><th>Property</th><th>Consistent Hashing</th><th>mod N</th></tr></thead>
          <tbody>
            <tr><td>Keys remapped on add</td><td><span class="badge badge-good">
 K/N</span></td><td><span class="badge badge-bad">
 K</span></td></tr>
            <tr><td>Load balance</td><td><span class="badge badge-good">Even (w/ vnodes)</span></td><td><span class="badge badge-neutral">Even</span></td></tr>
            <tr><td>Topology change cost</td><td><span class="badge badge-good">O(K/N)</span></td><td><span class="badge badge-bad">O(K)</span></td></tr>
            <tr><td>Implementation</td><td><span class="badge badge-neutral">Moderate</span></td><td><span class="badge badge-good">Trivial</span></td></tr>
            <tr><td>Used in</td><td>DynamoDB, Cassandra, Memcached</td><td>Simple caches</td></tr>
          </tbody>
        </table>
      </div>
    </div>
    <aside class="sidebar">
      <div class="eyebrow">Glossary</div>
      <dl>
        <div class="glossary-item" data-term="hash-ring"><dt>Hash Ring</dt><dd>A circular space [0, 2
) where both nodes and keys are positioned via a hash function.</dd></div>
        <div class="glossary-item" data-term="node"><dt>Node</dt><dd>A server or process responsible for a range of the hash ring.</dd></div>
        <div class="glossary-item" data-term="key"><dt>Key</dt><dd>A data identifier (e.g., cache key, row ID) hashed onto the ring.</dd></div>
        <div class="glossary-item" data-term="successor"><dt>Successor</dt><dd>The first node clockwise from a key's position 
 the node responsible for that key.</dd></div>
        <div class="glossary-item" data-term="partition"><dt>Partition</dt><dd>The arc of the ring between two consecutive nodes; all keys in this arc belong to the clockwise node.</dd></div>
        <div class="glossary-item" data-term="vnode"><dt>Virtual Node</dt><dd>Multiple hash positions per physical node for better load distribution.</dd></div>
      </dl>
    </aside>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
const CX = 170, CY = 170, R = 130;
const COLORS = [
  'var(--color-teal-6)', 'var(--color-indigo-6)', 'var(--color-violet-6)',
  'var(--color-coral-6)', 'var(--color-amber-7)', 'var(--color-teal-9)',
  'var(--color-indigo-9)', 'var(--color-violet-9)'
const NAMES = ['Node-A', 'Node-B', 'Node-C', 'Node-D', 'Node-E', 'Node-F', 'Node-G', 'Node-H'];
let nodes = [
  { name: 'Node-A', angle: 30 },
  { name: 'Node-B', angle: 150 },
  { name: 'Node-C', angle: 270 }
const KEYS = [
  { label: 'k1', angle: 60 },
  { label: 'k2', angle: 110 },
  { label: 'k3', angle: 200 },
  { label: 'k4', angle: 320 },
function toRad(d) { return (d - 90) * Math.PI / 180; }
function pos(angle, r) {
  return { x: CX + r * Math.cos(toRad(angle)), y: CY + r * Math.sin(toRad(angle)) };
function render() {
  const svg = document.getElementById('ringSvg');
  document.getElementById('nodeCount').textContent = `Nodes on ring: ${nodes.length}`;
  let html = '';
  // ring
  html += `<circle cx="${CX}" cy="${CY}" r="${R}" fill="none" stroke="var(--color-border-tertiary)" stroke-width="2.5" stroke-dasharray="6,4"/>`;
  // partition arcs
  const sorted = [...nodes].sort((a, b) => a.angle - b.angle);
  sorted.forEach((n, i) => {
    const next = sorted[(i + 1) % sorted.length];
    const start = n.angle, end = next.angle;
    const sa = toRad(start), ea = toRad(end < start ? end + 360 : end);
    const largeArc = ((end < start ? end + 360 : end) - start) > 180 ? 1 : 0;
    const p1 = pos(start, R), p2 = pos(end, R);
    html += `<path d="M ${p1.x} ${p1.y} A ${R} ${R} 0 ${largeArc} 1 ${p2.x} ${p2.y}" fill="none" stroke="${COLORS[i % COLORS.length]}" stroke-width="4" opacity=".3"/>`;
  });
  // keys
  KEYS.forEach(k => {
    const p = pos(k.angle, R);
    html += `<circle cx="${p.x}" cy="${p.y}" r="4" fill="var(--color-slate-7)"/>`;
    const lp = pos(k.angle, R + 18);
    html += `<text x="${lp.x}" y="${lp.y}" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="10" fill="var(--color-text-tertiary)" font-family="var(--font-mono)">${k.label}</text>`;
  });
  // nodes
  nodes.forEach((n, i) => {
    const p = pos(n.angle, R);
    html += `<circle cx="${p.x}" cy="${p.y}" r="12" fill="${COLORS[i % COLORS.length]}" stroke="var(--color-background-primary)" stroke-width="3">`;
    html += `<animate attributeName="r" from="6" to="12" dur=".3s" fill="freeze"/></circle>`;
    const lp = pos(n.angle, R - 26);
    html += `<text x="${lp.x}" y="${lp.y}" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="middle" font-size="10" font-weight="600" fill="${COLORS[i % COLORS.length]}">${n.name}</text>`;
  });
  // center label
  html += `<text x="${CX}" y="${CY - 6}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="11" font-weight="600" fill="var(--color-text-secondary)">Hash Ring</text>`;
  html += `<text x="${CX}" y="${CY + 10}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="10" fill="var(--color-text-tertiary)">[0, 2
)</text>`;
  svg.innerHTML = html;
function addNode() {
  if (nodes.length >= 8) return;
  const usedNames = new Set(nodes.map(n => n.name));
  const name = NAMES.find(n => !usedNames.has(n));
  const usedAngles = nodes.map(n => n.angle);
  let bestAngle = 0, bestDist = 0;
  for (let a = 0; a < 360; a += 5) {
    const minDist = Math.min(...usedAngles.map(ua => Math.min(Math.abs(a - ua), 360 - Math.abs(a - ua))));
    if (minDist > bestDist) { bestDist = minDist; bestAngle = a; }
  nodes.push({ name, angle: bestAngle });
  render();
function removeNode() {
  if (nodes.length <= 1) return;
  nodes.pop();
  render();
// Glossary hover
document.querySelectorAll('.term').forEach(el => {
  el.addEventListener('mouseenter', () => {
    const t = el.dataset.term;
    document.querySelectorAll('.glossary-item').forEach(g => {
      g.classList.toggle('active', g.dataset.term === t);
    });
  });
  el.addEventListener('mouseleave', () => {
    document.querySelectorAll('.glossary-item').forEach(g => g.classList.remove('active'));
  });
render();
</script>
</body>
</html>

const data = [
  { day: 'Mon', val: 8 }, { day: 'Tue', val: 11 }, { day: 'Wed', val: 14 },
  { day: 'Thu', val: 7 }, { day: 'Fri', val: 7 }
const maxVal = Math.max(...data.map(d => d.val));
const barW = 60, gap = 70, startX = 90;
const barsG = document.getElementById('bars');
const labelsG = document.getElementById('labels');
data.forEach((d, i) => {
  const x = startX + i * (barW + gap);
  const h = (d.val / maxVal) * 110;
  const y = 140 - h;
  const isPeak = d.val === maxVal;
  const color = isPeak ? 'var(--color-indigo-6)' : 'var(--color-sky-5)';
  barsG.innerHTML += `<rect x="${x}" y="${y}" width="${barW}" height="${h}" rx="4" fill="${color}" opacity=".85">
    <animate attributeName="height" from="0" to="${h}" dur=".4s" fill="freeze"/>
    <animate attributeName="y" from="140" to="${y}" dur=".4s" fill="freeze"/>
  </rect>`;
  barsG.innerHTML += `<text x="${x + barW/2}" y="${y - 6}" text-anchor="middle" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="${isPeak ? 'var(--color-indigo-9)' : 'var(--color-sky-9)'}" font-family="var(--font-mono)">${d.val}</text>`;
  labelsG.innerHTML += `<text x="${x + barW/2}" y="155" text-anchor="middle">${d.day}</text>`;

      <h3>Root Cause</h3>
      <p style="font-size:13px;">Deploy <code>sync-api@v2.14.1</code> at 13:58 removed the <code>idle_timeout</code> parameter from the connection pool config, causing connections to leak under sustained load.</p>

<span class="del">- max_lifetime: 300s</span><br>
<span class="add">+ # timeout handled by upstream</span><br>
<span class="add">+ max_lifetime: 300s</span>

function toggle(el) {

function getAvatarColor(initials) {
  let h = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < initials.length; i++) h = initials.charCodeAt(i) + ((h << 5) - h);
  return AVATAR_COLORS[Math.abs(h) % AVATAR_COLORS.length];
function calcPoints(colKey) {
  return TICKETS.filter(t => t.col === colKey).reduce((s, t) => s + SIZES[t.size], 0);
function renderBoard() {
  const board = document.getElementById('board');
  board.innerHTML = '';
  COLUMNS.forEach(col => {
    const colEl = document.createElement('div');
    colEl.className = `column ${col.cls}`;
    const pts = calcPoints(col.key);
    colEl.innerHTML = `
      <div class="col-header">
        <span class="col-title">${col.label}</span>
        <span class="col-pts">${pts} pts</span>
      </div>
    `;
    const body = document.createElement('div');
    body.className = 'col-body';
    body.dataset.col = col.key;
    body.addEventListener('dragover', e => { e.preventDefault(); body.classList.add('drag-over'); });
    body.addEventListener('dragleave', () => body.classList.remove('drag-over'));
    body.addEventListener('drop', e => {
      e.preventDefault(); body.classList.remove('drag-over');
      const tid = e.dataTransfer.getData('text/plain');
      const ticket = TICKETS.find(t => t.id === tid);
      if (ticket) { ticket.col = col.key; renderBoard(); }
    });
    TICKETS.filter(t => t.col === col.key).forEach(t => {
      const card = document.createElement('div');
      card.className = `ticket type-${t.type}`;
      card.draggable = true;
      card.dataset.id = t.id;
      card.addEventListener('dragstart', e => {
        e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', t.id);
        card.classList.add('dragging');
      });
      card.addEventListener('dragend', () => card.classList.remove('dragging'));
      card.innerHTML = `
        <div class="top-row">
          <span class="tid">${t.id}</span>
          <div class="assignee" style="background:${getAvatarColor(t.assignee)}">${t.assignee}</div>
        </div>
        <div class="title">${t.title}</div>
        <div class="bottom-row">
          <span class="type-badge type-${t.type}">${t.type}</span>
          <span class="size-pill">${t.size}</span>
        </div>
      `;
      body.appendChild(card);
    });
    colEl.appendChild(body);
    board.appendChild(colEl);
  });
function copyMarkdown() {
  let md = `# Triage Board 
 Q1 Sprint 6\n\n`;
  COLUMNS.forEach(col => {
    const items = TICKETS.filter(t => t.col === col.key);
    const pts = items.reduce((s, t) => s + SIZES[t.size], 0);
    md += `## ${col.label} (${pts} pts)\n\n`;
    md += `| ID | Title | Type | Size | Assignee |\n`;
    md += `|----|-------|------|------|----------|\n`;
    items.forEach(t => {
      md += `| ${t.id} | ${t.title} | ${t.type} | ${t.size} | ${t.assignee} |\n`;
    });
    md += `\n`;
  });
  navigator.clipboard.writeText(md).then(() => {
    const btn = document.querySelector('.copy-btn');
    btn.textContent = '
 Copied!';
    btn.classList.add('copied');
    setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = '
 Copy as Markdown'; btn.classList.remove('copied'); }, 2000);
  });
renderBoard();
</script>

const FLAGS = [
  { group: 'Onboarding', flags: [
    { key: 'onboarding_wizard_v2', name: 'Onboarding Wizard V2', desc: 'New multi-step wizard flow for first-time users', enabled: true, rollout: 100 },

  ]},
  { group: 'Sync', flags: [
    { key: 'realtime_sync', name: 'Realtime Sync', desc: 'Enable WebSocket-based realtime document sync', enabled: true, rollout: 80 },

  ]},

    { key: 'debug_panel', name: 'Debug Panel', desc: 'Show debug overlay with request timings and state', enabled: true, rollout: 100 },
    { key: 'canary_deploy', name: 'Canary Deploy Gate', desc: 'Route canary traffic to experimental backend instances', enabled: false, rollout: 5 },
  ]},
let original = {};
let current = {};
function init() {
  FLAGS.forEach(g => g.flags.forEach(f => { original[f.key] = { enabled: f.enabled, rollout: f.rollout }; current[f.key] = { enabled: f.enabled, rollout: f.rollout }; }));
  render();
function render() {
  const container = document.getElementById('flagGroups');
  container.innerHTML = FLAGS.map(g => `
    <div class="group">
      <div class="group-header" onclick="toggleGroup(this)">
        <span class="chevron open">
</span>
        <span class="eyebrow">${g.group}</span>
      </div>
      <div class="group-body">
        ${g.flags.map(f => renderFlag(f)).join('')}
      </div>
    </div>
  `).join('');
  updateChangeCount();
function renderFlag(f) {
  const depOff = f.depends && !current[f.depends]?.enabled;
  return `
    <div class="flag-card ${depOff ? 'warning' : ''}">
      <label class="toggle">
        <input type="checkbox" ${current[f.key].enabled ? 'checked' : ''} onchange="toggleFlag('${f.key}', this.checked)">
        <span class="slider"></span>
      </label>
      <div class="flag-info">
        <div class="flag-name">${f.name}</div>
        <div class="flag-desc">${f.desc}</div>
        ${f.rollout !== undefined ? `<div class="rollout"><input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="${current[f.key].rollout}" oninput="setRollout('${f.key}', this.value, this)"><span class="rollout-val">${current[f.key].rollout}%</span></div>` : ''}
        ${depOff ? `<span class="warning-badge">
 Requires "${f.depends}" enabled</span>` : ''}
      </div>
    </div>`;
function toggleFlag(key, val) { current[key].enabled = val; render(); }
function setRollout(key, val, el) { current[key].rollout = parseInt(val); el.nextElementSibling.textContent = val + '%'; updateChangeCount(); }
function toggleGroup(el) {
  el.querySelector('.chevron').classList.toggle('open');
  el.nextElementSibling.classList.toggle('collapsed');
function updateChangeCount() {
  let count = 0;
  Object.keys(current).forEach(k => { if (current[k].enabled !== original[k].enabled || current[k].rollout !== original[k].rollout) count++; });
  document.getElementById('changeCount').textContent = count + ' change' + (count !== 1 ? 's' : '');
function copyDiff() {
  const diff = {};
  Object.keys(current).forEach(k => {
    if (current[k].enabled !== original[k].enabled || current[k].rollout !== original[k].rollout) diff[k] = current[k];
  });
  const output = JSON.stringify(diff, null, 2);
  const el = document.getElementById('diffOutput');
  el.textContent = output || '// No changes';
  el.style.display = 'block';
  navigator.clipboard?.writeText(output);
function resetAll() {
  Object.keys(original).forEach(k => { current[k] = { ...original[k] }; });
  document.getElementById('diffOutput').style.display = 'none';
  render();
init();

<script>
const DEFAULT_TEMPLATE = `You are a helpful customer support agent for {{company_name}}.
The customer's name is {{customer_name}} and their issue is: {{issue_summary}}.
Draft a professional, empathetic reply that:
1. Acknowledges their frustration
2. Provides a clear resolution path
3. Offers a {{compensation_type}} if appropriate
Keep the tone warm but concise. Sign off as {{agent_name}}.`;
const SLOTS = ['company_name', 'customer_name', 'issue_summary', 'compensation_type', 'agent_name'];
const SAMPLES = [
  { label: 'Sample A 
 Billing Dispute', values: { company_name: 'CloudSync Pro', customer_name: 'Sarah M.', issue_summary: 'was charged twice for the annual plan renewal', compensation_type: '15% discount on next renewal', agent_name: 'Alex from Support' }},
  { label: 'Sample B 
 Feature Request', values: { company_name: 'DevToolkit', customer_name: 'James K.', issue_summary: 'needs dark mode for the dashboard but it is not available yet', compensation_type: 'early access invite', agent_name: 'Mia from Product' }},
  { label: 'Sample C 
 Downtime Report', values: { company_name: 'StatusPage.io', customer_name: 'Chen Wei', issue_summary: 'experienced 4 hours of API downtime impacting their production services', compensation_type: 'service credit', agent_name: 'Jordan from Engineering' }},
function init() {
  document.getElementById('promptEditor').value = DEFAULT_TEMPLATE;
  renderSlots();
  updatePreviews();
function renderSlots() {
  document.getElementById('slotPills').innerHTML = SLOTS.map(s =>
    `<span class="slot-pill" onclick="insertSlot('${s}')">{{${s}}}</span>`
  ).join('');
function insertSlot(name) {
  const ta = document.getElementById('promptEditor');
  const start = ta.selectionStart;
  const text = ta.value;
  const insert = `{{${name}}}`;
  ta.value = text.slice(0, start) + insert + text.slice(ta.selectionEnd);
  ta.selectionStart = ta.selectionEnd = start + insert.length;
  ta.focus();
  updatePreviews();
function updatePreviews() {
  const template = document.getElementById('promptEditor').value;
  const chars = template.length;
  document.getElementById('charCount').textContent = chars + ' chars';
  document.getElementById('tokenCount').textContent = '~' + Math.ceil(chars / 4) + ' tokens';
  document.getElementById('previewCards').innerHTML = SAMPLES.map(s => {
    let filled = template;
    Object.entries(s.values).forEach(([k, v]) => {
      filled = filled.replace(new RegExp(`\\{\\{${k}\\}\\}`, 'g'), `<span class="highlight">${v}</span>`);
    });
    // Highlight remaining unfilled slots
    filled = filled.replace(/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g, '<span class="highlight">
</span>');
    return `<div class="preview-card"><div class="preview-card-header">${s.label}</div><div class="preview-card-body">${filled}</div></div>`;
  }).join('');
function copyPrompt() {
  navigator.clipboard?.writeText(document.getElementById('promptEditor').value);
function resetPrompt() {
  document.getElementById('promptEditor').value = DEFAULT_TEMPLATE;
  updatePreviews();
init();
</script>

TRAE-dynamic-ui/examples/INDEX.md# Dynamic UI 
 Examples Index
20 reference HTML widgets covering the most common visual scenarios developers encounter when working with AI assistants. **Use them as layout and interaction blueprints 
 copy the technique, generate fresh content.**
## How to use
1. Match your task to the closest scenario below
2. Read the matching example file 
 focus on CSS structure, layout grid, color usage, and interaction patterns
3. Adapt the layout for your content. Change data, labels, colors 
 keep the structural approach.
4. **Do not copy content verbatim. Copy the structural approach, then fill with task-specific data.**

TRAE-dynamic-ui/referencesTRAE-dynamic-ui/references/chart-guide.md# Chart & Map Guide
## Chart.js (Inline & Panel)
Canvas in div with explicit height + `position: relative`. Set `responsive: true`, `maintainAspectRatio: false`. Load UMD via CDN.
Disable default legend, build custom HTML legend. Canvas cannot resolve CSS variables 
 use hardcoded hex from the color palette.
```html
<div style="position:relative; height:300px">
  <canvas id="myChart"></canvas>
</div>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/chart.js"></script>
<script>
  new Chart(document.getElementById('myChart'), { /* config */ });
</script>
## ECharts (Panel preferred)
Best for complex, interactive charts with auto-resize. Load via CDN.
```html
<div id="chart" style="width:100%; height:400px"></div>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/echarts@5/dist/echarts.min.js"></script>
<script>
  const chart = echarts.init(document.getElementById('chart'));
  chart.setOption({ /* config */ });
  window.addEventListener('resize', () => chart.resize());
</script>
Key advantages over Chart.js for panel mode:
- Richer chart types (treemap, sunburst, sankey, gauge)
- Built-in tooltip, legend, zoom interactions
- Auto-resize with `chart.resize()`
- Better suited for dashboard-style multi-chart layouts
## D3 Choropleth (Geographic Maps)
Never invent coordinates. Three topology sources:
- `us-atlas` 
 US states/counties
- `world-atlas` 
 countries
- `datamaps` 
 alternative country shapes
Always `web_fetch` the topology URL first to verify availability.
Load D3 + topojson via CDN:
```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3@7"></script>
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/topojson-client@3"></script>
## Interactive Explainer
HTML with sliders, buttons, live displays. No card wrapper. Use `sendPrompt()` for follow-up questions (not data export).
Range slider pattern:
```html
<input type="range" min="0" max="100" value="50"
  oninput="update(this.value)">
<span id="display">50</span>
TRAE-dynamic-ui/references/design-system.md# Shared Design System
All visual output 
 inline or panel 
 shares this design foundation.
## Philosophy
- **Seamless**: Integrate visually with the IDE 
 match its rhythm, not fight it.
- **Expressive**: Use color boldly to encode meaning, create hierarchy, and make information scannable. Flat 
 boring.
- **Compact**: Show the essential visually. Explain the rest in text.
- **Separation**: Text goes in your response, visuals go in the tool 
 all explanatory text, descriptions, introductions, and summaries must be written as normal response text OUTSIDE the tool call. The tool output should contain ONLY the visual element.
## Visual Richness 
 Be Bold With Color
**Default is colorful, not monochrome.** A widget that is entirely black-white-gray is visually dead. Always apply at least one accent color.
### Default Accent
When you need a general-purpose accent (links, highlights, primary actions, active states), use **sky** (`--color-sky-*`). It is neutral, professional, and works in both light/dark modes.
For secondary accent, pair with **indigo** or **violet**.
### Color Usage Patterns (apply these actively)
- **KPI / hero numbers**: Use accent color (sky-60 or indigo-60) for the number, secondary text for the label
- **Section eyebrows**: 11px monospace uppercase labels above headings 
 use `--color-text-tertiary` or a muted accent
- **Card left accent bar**: A 3-4px colored left border on cards to indicate category (`border-left: 3px solid var(--color-sky-5)`)
- **Status indicators**: green=success, amber=warning, coral=error 
 use filled dots or pill badges with light fill + strong text
- **Flow/architecture nodes**: Each layer/category gets its own color ramp. Never make all nodes the same gray.
- **Interactive hover**: Background shifts from transparent to `--color-background-overlay-l2` with accent border
- **Progress / metrics**: Use colored bars, not just numbers. A horizontal bar in sky/mint/amber instantly communicates magnitude.
- **Tables**: Alternate row backgrounds using `--color-background-overlay-l1`. Header row uses subtle accent background.
- **Tags / badges / pills**: Light fill (ramp-10) + strong text (ramp-70). e.g. `background: var(--color-sky-1); color: var(--color-sky-7)`
### Allowed Visual Embellishments
You ARE encouraged to use:
- Subtle `box-shadow` for elevated cards: `var(--shadow-sm)` or `var(--shadow-md)`
- Colored left/top borders on cards and sections
- Dot/circle decorative elements for timelines and step indicators
- Animated transitions on hover/click (transform, opacity, background-color)
- Colored icon badges (small colored circles behind icons)
### What Still Not To Do
- **No gradient backgrounds** 
 no `linear-gradient`, `radial-gradient`, or any multi-color gradient fills on containers, headers, or hero sections. Backgrounds must be flat solid colors using CSS variables.
- No neon glow, no heavy drop shadows, no 3D effects
- No full-bleed colored backgrounds (the host provides outer bg)
- No mesh/noise texture images
- No multiple competing saturated colors fighting for attention (pick 1 primary + 1 secondary accent)
## CSS Variables
**Backgrounds**: `--color-background-primary` (white), `-secondary` (surfaces), `-tertiary` (page bg), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning`
**Text**: `--color-text-primary` (black), `-secondary` (muted), `-tertiary` (hints), `-info`, `-danger`, `-success`, `-warning`
**Borders**: `--color-border-tertiary` (0.15
, default), `-secondary` (0.3
, hover), `-primary` (0.4
), semantic `-info/-danger/-success/-warning`
**Typography**: `--font-sans`, `--font-serif`, `--font-mono`
**Layout**: `--border-radius-md` (8px), `--border-radius-lg` (10px), `--border-radius-xl` (12px)
All auto-adapt to light/dark mode.
## Color Palette
10 color ramps, 10 stops each. Use them generously 
 they exist to be used, not admired in a table.
| Ramp | Purpose suggestion | Light fill | Strong accent | Text on fill |
|------|-------------------|-----------|---------------|-------------|
| coral | Error, alerts, hot metrics | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |
| amber | Warnings, in-progress, medium priority | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |
| lime | Success secondary, growth, positive delta | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |
| mint | Success primary, complete, healthy | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |
| teal | Info secondary, data, neutral-positive | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |
| sky | **Primary accent**, links, active, info | 1-2 | 5-6 | 7-8 |
| indigo | **Secondary accent**, special, premium | 1-2 | 5-6 | 7-8 |
| violet | Creative, AI-related, unique | 1-2 | 5-6 | 7-8 |
| magenta | Attention, new, promotional | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |
| slate | Neutral, structural, disabled | 1-2 | 6-7 | 8-9 |

**Quick rules**:
- Every widget MUST use at least 1 non-gray color ramp
- Group related items by color; different categories = different ramps
- Light mode: 1-2 fill + 6 stroke + 8 title text
- Dark mode: 8 fill + 2 stroke + 1 title text
- Text on colored fills: use same ramp 8-9 (light) or 1-2 (dark). Never plain black/gray.
**Color assignment**: Encode meaning, not sequence. Group by category. Use gray for neutral/structural only 
 never as the sole color.
## SVG Pre-built Classes
- `class="t"` = sans 14px primary text
- `class="ts"` = sans 12px secondary text
- `class="th"` = sans 14px medium(500) heading text
- `class="box"` = neutral rect
- `class="node"` = clickable group
- `class="arr"` = arrow line
- `class="leader"` = dashed leader line
- `class="c-{ramp}"` = colored node (c-sky, c-teal, etc). Apply to `<g>` or shape, NOT paths.
## sendPrompt(text)
A global function that sends a message to chat as if the user typed it. Use for follow-up questions, not for data export.
## Dark Mode
Dark mode is mandatory 
 every color must work in both modes:
- In SVG: use pre-built color classes (`c-sky`, `c-teal`, `c-amber`, etc.) for colored nodes.
- In SVG: every `<text>` needs a class (`t`, `ts`, `th`).
- In HTML: always use CSS variables for text. Never hardcode colors.
## Typography
- Two weights only: 400 regular, 600 bold.
- h1=18px, h2=16px, h3=14px, body=14px. Never use 700.
- **Sentence case** always. Never Title Case, never ALL CAPS (except eyebrow labels).
- No mid-sentence bolding. Entity names go in code style, not bold.
- font-sans / font-serif / font-mono via CSS variables.
- Use `--font-serif` for hero/page titles in panel mode to create visual distinction.
- Use `--font-mono` at 11px with letter-spacing 0.06em for eyebrow labels, category tags, and metadata.
## Visual Signature Elements
These recurring patterns give our widgets a cohesive, recognizable look. Use them:
### Eyebrow Labels
Small monospace uppercase text above section headings 
 our signature rhythm marker:
```css
.eyebrow {
  font-family: var(--font-mono);
  font-size: 11px;
  letter-spacing: 0.06em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--color-text-tertiary);
  margin-bottom: 6px;
### Accent Bars
Colored left borders on cards to signal category:
```css
.card-accent { border-left: 3px solid var(--color-sky-5); }
.card-accent-warn { border-left: 3px solid var(--color-amber-5); }
.card-accent-error { border-left: 3px solid var(--color-coral-5); }
### Status Pills
Compact colored badges:
```css
.pill { display: inline-flex; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: var(--border-radius-full); font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; }
.pill-success { background: var(--color-mint-1); color: var(--color-mint-7); }
.pill-warning { background: var(--color-amber-1); color: var(--color-amber-7); }
.pill-error { background: var(--color-coral-1); color: var(--color-coral-7); }
.pill-info { background: var(--color-sky-1); color: var(--color-sky-7); }
### Metric Cards
Numbers that pop:
```css
.metric-value { font-size: 28px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--color-sky-6); line-height: 1.1; }
.metric-label { font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-text-secondary); margin-top: 4px; }
.metric-delta-up { color: var(--color-mint-6); }
.metric-delta-down { color: var(--color-coral-6); }
## Universal Prohibitions
- No emoji 
 use CSS shapes or SVG paths
- No neon glow, heavy drop shadows, blur filters, or 3D perspective effects
- No dark/colored backgrounds on the outermost container (transparent only 
 host provides the bg)
- No `position: fixed`
- No hardcoded colors (use CSS variables or palette classes)
- No `font-size` below 11px
- No comments in output (waste tokens, break streaming)
- **CDN allowlist (CSP-enforced)**: `cdnjs.cloudflare.com`, `esm.sh`, `cdn.jsdelivr.net`, `unpkg.com` only.
TRAE-dynamic-ui/references/inline-mode.md# Inline Mode Rules
Inline mode renders compact visuals embedded directly in the chat response. Content appears alongside the AI's text, so it must be concise and streaming-friendly.
## Hard Limits
- No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` 
 content fragments only.
- Height is auto-fit but the host enforces a MAX_HEIGHT cap.
- Single SVG or compact HTML fragment per tool call.
- `<style>` blocks 
15 lines. Prefer inline `style="..."`.
- No nested scrolling 
 content must fit without scroll.
- No `position: fixed`.
- No tabs, carousels, or `display: none` (not streaming-friendly).
## Complexity Budget
- SVG: 
5 nodes per diagram, viewBox 680px fixed width.
- Horizontal tier: 
4 boxes at full width (~140px each). 5+ boxes 
 shrink to 
110px OR wrap to 2 rows OR split into overview + detail.
- Colors: 
2 color ramps per diagram. If colors encode meaning, add a 1-line legend.
- Scripts: tail-loaded only, CDN allowlist applies.
- Box subtitles: 
5 words. Detail goes in sendPrompt or prose 
 not the box.
## Streaming Output Order (Hard Rule)
Output streams token-by-token. **Structure code so styles load BEFORE content:**
- **HTML order**: `<style>` FIRST 
 content HTML 
 `<script>` LAST. Never reverse this.
- **SVG order**: `<defs>` (markers) 
 visual elements immediately.
- Prefer inline `style="..."` over `<style>` blocks for inline mode (keeps style closer to element).
- Gradients, shadows, and blur flash during streaming DOM diffs. Use solid flat fills.
- No `display:none` toggling 
 elements should render progressively.
**Why**: Streaming means user sees partial output. If styles come after content, user sees unstyled flash 
 unacceptable.
## Output Principles
- Text explanation goes OUTSIDE the tool call, in your response text.
- The tool output contains ONLY the visual element.
- Background must be transparent 
 host provides the background color.
- The widget container is `display: block; width: 100%`. No wrapper div needed.
## UI Components
**Tokens**: Borders = `0.5px solid var(--color-border-tertiary)`. Cards = white bg, 0.5px border, border-radius-lg, padding 1rem 1.25rem. Buttons: transparent bg, 0.5px border, sendPrompt gets 
 arrow.
**Metric cards**: muted 13px label, 24px/500 number. bg-base-secondary, no border, radius-md, padding 1rem. Grid of 2-4.
**Layout**: Editorial = no card wrapper. Card = single raised card. No tables in tool output.
**Round every displayed number** 
 use Math.round(), .toFixed(n), or Intl.NumberFormat.
**Corners**: `border-radius: var(--border-radius-md)` (or `--border-radius-lg` for cards) in HTML. In SVG, `rx="4"` default. No rounded corners on single-sided borders.
**Icon sizing**: emoji=16px, SVG icons=16px
16px. Decorative icons 24px max.
## Modules
After loading inline mode, pick the closest sub-module:
- **diagram** 
 SVG flowcharts, structural diagrams, illustrative diagrams
- **mockup** 
 UI mockups, forms, cards, dashboards
- **interactive** 
 interactive explainers with controls
- **chart** 
 charts, data analysis, geographic maps (Chart.js, D3)
- **art** 
 illustration and generative art
## Compare Options
Side-by-side card grid. Recommended option gets 2px info border + badge.
## Data Record
Single raised card. Avatar/initials circle for people.
## Mockup Presentation
Contained mockups need background surface. Full-width mockups don't.
TRAE-dynamic-ui/references/panel-mode.md# Panel Mode Rules
Panel mode renders large, complex visuals in a dedicated Webview Panel. Content can scroll, contain multiple sections, and support rich interactions 
 no height cap.
## Streaming Output Order (Hard Rule)
Output streams token-by-token. **Structure code so styles load BEFORE content:**
1. **`<style>` block FIRST** 
 all CSS rules at the top, before any HTML content.
2. **HTML content SECOND** 
 with styles already parsed, elements render correctly immediately.
3. **`<script>` block LAST** 
 scripts never block visual rendering.
This prevents the "flash of unstyled content" during streaming. Never put `<style>` after HTML content.
## Key Differences from Inline
- No height limit 
 supports vertical scrolling.
- Multi-section page structure allowed (header / main / sidebar / footer).
- Complex scripts allowed (ECharts, D3, drag-and-drop, etc.).
- `<style>` blocks have no line limit.
- Page-level layout patterns (grid, flexbox columns) encouraged.
## Still Required (Shared Rules)
- Use framework CSS variables for all colors (auto theme adaptation).
- Background transparent 
 framework shell provides the base color.
- sendPrompt() is available for "ask AI to process this" interactions.
- CDN allowlist still enforced (CSP).
- **No DOCTYPE, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>`** 
 framework shell wraps the content.
- Dark mode must work.
## Page Structure
Panel content should follow a clear section hierarchy:
```html
<!-- Header area -->
<div class="panel-header">
  <h1>Title</h1>
  <p class="subtitle">Subtitle or description</p>
</div>
<!-- Main content sections -->
<section class="panel-section">
  <h2>Section heading</h2>
  <!-- Section content -->
</section>
<!-- Repeat sections as needed -->
## Layout Patterns
Pick the closest pattern for your content:
**Report**: Title bar 
 KPI metric grid 
 chart area 
 event timeline 
 summary
- Best for: weekly reports, project status, post-mortems
**Comparison**: Title 
 side-by-side card grid 
 summary table 
 recommendation
- Best for: tech selection, proposal review, A/B analysis
**Dashboard**: Filter bar 
 multi-chart grid (2
2 or 3-col) 
 detail table
- Best for: monitoring overview, analytics, metrics deep-dive
**Timeline**: Title 
 vertical timeline with event cards 
 milestones
- Best for: project history, incident timeline, changelog
**Kanban**: Column headers 
 draggable cards in columns 
 status summary
- Best for: task management, workflow stages, content pipeline
## Visual Specifications
- Container: `max-width: 960px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 32px 24px`
- Cards: white bg + `1px solid var(--color-border-tertiary)` + `border-radius: var(--border-radius-lg)` + `padding: 1.25rem`
- Section gap: 32px (use `gap` or `margin-bottom`)
- Typography: h1=24px/600, h2=18px/600, h3=16px/500, body=14px/400
- Dividers: `1px solid var(--color-border-tertiary)`
- KPI numbers: 28px/600, labels: 13px/400 muted
## Interaction Rules
- Editor-type panels **must** include an "Export" button.
- Export via clipboard (`navigator.clipboard.writeText`) or file download (`Blob` + `URL.createObjectURL`).
- sendPrompt(text) is for "let AI continue processing" only (e.g., "help me refine this"), NOT for export.
- Complex interactions (drag, sort, filter) implemented in `<script>`.
- Charts: prefer ECharts for rich chart types and responsive resize.
## Preview Behavior
When mode="panel", the chat flow shows:
- A height-limited thumbnail preview of the content.
- An "Open in panel" button.
- Clicking the button opens the full content in a dedicated Webview Panel (same sandbox framework, no height cap).
TRAE-dynamic-ui/references/svg-guide.md# SVG Drawing Guide
## SVG Setup
`<svg width="100%" viewBox="0 0 680 H">` 
 680px fixed width, flexible height. The 680 is load-bearing 
 do not change. Safe area: x=40 to x=640.
## ViewBox Safety Checklist
1. Find lowest element: max(y+height). Set viewBox height = that + 40px.
2. All content within x=0 to x=680.
3. `text-anchor="end"` extends LEFT 
 check overflow.
4. Never negative x or y coordinates.
5. Flowcharts: check box pairs have 20px+ gap.
**One SVG per tool call.**
## Arrow Marker
Include in every SVG `<defs>`:
```xml
<defs><marker id="arrow" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="8" refY="5" markerWidth="6" markerHeight="6" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M2 1L8 5L2 9" fill="none" stroke="context-stroke" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"/></marker></defs>
## Font Calibration
At 14px, ~8px per Latin char. At 12px, ~7px per char. Verify: (text_width + 2
padding) < box_width.
## Stroke Width
1px for borders/edges. Connector paths need `fill="none"`.
## Diagram Types
**Two critical rules**:
1. Arrow intersection check 
 never cross unrelated boxes.
2. Box width from longest label: max(title_chars
8, subtitle_chars
7)+24.
**Pick by intent**: Reference diagrams (flowchart, structural) vs Intuition diagrams (illustrative). Route on the verb, not the noun.
### Flowchart
60px min between boxes, 24px padding inside, 12px text-to-edge. Every `<text>` inside box needs `dominant-baseline="central"`. Max 4-5 nodes per diagram. Cycles 
 HTML stepper, not ring.
### Structural Diagram
Large rounded rects as containers, smaller rects inside. 20px min padding inside containers. Max 2-3 nesting levels. Use distinct color ramps for nested levels.
### Illustrative Diagram
For building intuition. Physical subjects = simplified cross-sections. Abstract subjects = spatial metaphors. Color encodes intensity not category. Shapes are freeform. Layout follows subject geometry. One gradient permitted for continuous physical property. Interactive preferred over static.

TRAE-generate-mini-app/scriptsTRAE-generate-mini-app/scripts/init-template.js#!/usr/bin/env node
const originalEmit = process.emit;
process.emit = function (name, data, ...args) {
  if (name === 'warning' && typeof data === 'object' && data.name === 'DeprecationWarning' && data.message.includes('punycode')) {
